claims.claim: Environments set runtime, compute, libraries and resources; a workspace default environment can be changed only by workspace admins.
Quick mode installs at session start adding one to three minutes; Full mode is recommended for pipelines and scheduled runs.
V-Order is off by default in new workspaces (writeHeavy); write cost around 15%; table property, writer option and session default; spark.sql.parquet.vorder.enable removed in Runtime 1.3+.
New workspaces default to writeHeavy; readHeavyForPBI enables V-Order.

concept_html:
An environment is a Fabric item that fixes what a Spark session starts with: the runtime version, compute settings, libraries and small resource files. Attach it to notebooks and Spark job definitions, or make it the workspace default so every notebook set to "Workspace default" inherits it. Once an environment is the workspace default, only workspace admins can change its contents.

Libraries publish in one of two modes (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026):

  • Quick mode installs libraries when each session starts. It is flexible, and it adds one to three minutes to start-up.
  • Full mode builds a snapshot of the dependencies once. Microsoft recommends Full mode for pipelines, scheduled runs and shared workloads that need reproducible environments. It is the Fabric equivalent of the lock file in lesson B6-L3.

Resource profiles set a tested group of Spark and Delta settings with one property. New workspaces default to writeHeavy, tuned for ingestion. readHeavyForSpark and readHeavyForPBI suit read-heavy work.

V-Order is a Fabric write-time layout for Parquet files. It keeps files standard, open Parquet, and speeds up reads, especially for Power BI Direct Lake and the SQL engines. The cost is slower writes: Learn cites around 15% on average. Since the writeHeavy default, V-Order is off by default in new workspaces (spark.sql.parquet.vorder.default=false).

Turn it on where reads dominate, at the narrowest useful level:

  • per table: TBLPROPERTIES("delta.parquet.vorder.enabled" = "true"), the best choice for gold tables that Power BI reads,
  • per write: the DataFrame option parquet.vorder.enabled,
  • per session: spark.sql.parquet.vorder.default, or the readHeavyForPBI profile, which enables it.

In Runtime 1.3 and later the older spark.sql.parquet.vorder.enable setting is removed. Code copied from older posts that sets it does nothing.

exercises.prompt: Write `write_gold(df, table)` that overwrites a gold Delta table with V-Order enabled for this write, using the DataFrame writer option `parquet.vorder.enabled` set to `"true"`. Do not change the session-wide default.
exercises.prompt_html: Write write_gold(df, table) that overwrites a gold Delta table with V-Order enabled for this write, using the DataFrame writer option parquet.vorder.enabled set to "true". Do not change the session-wide default.
exercises.solution:
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame


def write_gold(df: DataFrame, table: str) -> None:
    """Overwrite a read-heavy gold table with V-Order for this write only.

    Args:
        df: Gold rows.
        table: Target table, such as lh.gold.sales_by_region.
    """
    df.write.mode("overwrite").option("parquet.vorder.enabled", "true").saveAsTable(table)

title: Environments, resource profiles and V-Order
why_html: A team moved its gold layer to a new Fabric workspace and noticed Power BI reports running noticeably slower than before. The old workspace had V-Order on for every write. The new one used the writeHeavy default, with V-Order off. Setting delta.parquet.vorder.enabled on the dozen gold tables, and optimising them once, restored read performance without slowing bronze and silver ingestion.
